target_moa.text: Precise anticonvulsant mechanism unknown; thought to act by potentiation of GABAergic (and possibly glutamatergic) neurotransmission, with indirect effects via inhibition of cytochrome P450 activity.

modality.text: Small molecule (aromatic allylic alcohol / pentanol derivative)

citations.quote: STP is an aromatic allylic alcohol. It is a new molecular entity and it is structurally unrelated to other drugs approved for the treatment of seizures.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=10% and more than placebo): somnolence, decreased appetite, agitation, ataxia, weight decreased, hypotonia, nausea, tremor, dysarthria, insomnia. Somnolence 67% vs 23% placebo; decreased appetite 46% vs 10%; decreased weight 27% vs 6%; neutropenia 13% (none on placebo); thrombocytopenia 12% vs 3%.

citations.quote: Adverse reactions that occurred in at least 10% of DIACOMIT-treated patients and more frequently than on placebo were somnolence, decreased appetite, agitation, ataxia, weight decreased, hypotonia, nausea, tremor, dysarthria, and insomnia. (6.1)
the incidence of somnolence was 67% in DIACOMIT-treated patients, compared to 23% in patients on placebo.

the incidence of decreased appetite was 46% in DIACOMIT-treated patients, compared to 10% in patients on placebo. The incidence of decreased weight was 27% in DIACOMIT-treated patients, compared to 6% in patients on placebo.

The incidence of neutropenia was 13% in STP-treated patients, and neutropenia was not observed in any placebo-treated patient. Thrombocytopenia was observed in 12% of STP-treated patients, compared to 3% in placebo-treated patients.
